summary: This informational document registers the media type audio/mobile-xmf. Mobile XMF is a compact format developed by the MIDI Manufacturers Association and the Association of Musical Electronics Industry for high-quality synthetic audio in mobile music downloading and messaging.

plainLanguage.summary: This gives a name tag to a small music file format designed for phones, so email and web programs know what kind of file it is.

subtitle: Register a MIME type for compact mobile music files.

tldr.problem: Mobile XMF is a compact audio format for synthetic music created by MIDI standards bodies, but without a registered MIME type, email and web programs cannot identify or handle these files correctly.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4723 registers the MIME type audio/mobile-xmf and specifies optional parameters for file revision, playback resource requirements, and other metadata.
tldr.outcome: Mobile applications and mail clients can now properly recognize and process Mobile XMF files.

today: RFC 4723 is an Informational RFC published in December 2006 and has not been obsoleted. It provides the official MIME type registration for Mobile XMF files.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Mobile XMF is a compact audio format designed specifically for mobile devices. It was developed jointly by the MIDI Manufacturers Association (MMA) and the Association of Musical Electronics Industry (AMEI) to enable high-quality synthetic music on phones, PDAs, and similar devices.

Mobile XMF encapsulates two technologies: SP-MIDI (Scalable Polyphony MIDI) for music sequences, and Mobile DLS (Downloadable Sounds) for instrument definitions. The format is much smaller than standard MIDI files, making it ideal for music downloading and messaging on bandwidth-limited mobile networks. However, without a MIME type registration, systems had no standard way to identify and process these files.
sections.plainLanguage: Mobile XMF is a very small, high-quality music format made for phones and tablets. This RFC gives it an official name tag so systems know what to do with it.

sections.title: The audio/mobile-xmf MIME Type
sections.content:
RFC 4723 registers the media type audio/mobile-xmf. This type has no required parameters, but supports three optional ones. The revision parameter carries the Mobile XMF file type revision ID from the XMF Meta File format. The prl (playback resource list) parameter describes which instrument resources are included in the file as two-digit hexadecimal codes.

The minimum-pr and total-pr parameters indicate playback resource requirements. These parameters help devices determine if they have enough memory and processing power to play the file. The parameters are encoded as sequences of hexadecimal digits and follow specific ordering requirements tied to the prl parameter.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIME type is audio/mobile-xmf. It can include optional notes like the file version and how much memory is needed to play the music.

sections.title: File Format and Transport
sections.content:
Mobile XMF files are stored in XMF file format, which is based on the XMF Meta File Format Specification v2.00. The format is binary and contains both the music sequence (SP-MIDI) and the instrument definitions (Mobile DLS) in a single file.

For transport over non-binary protocols like email, Base64 encoding is recommended. The RFC specifies magic numbers (the first twelve bytes of a Mobile XMF file are fixed: \\130\\115\\106\\137\\062\\056\\060\\060\\000\\000\\000\\002), allowing systems to identify the file type by its header. File extensions are typically .mxmf, and the Macintosh file type code is also mxmf.
sections.plainLanguage: Mobile XMF files are binary (computer code), so for email they need to be converted to Base64 text. The file starts with a special signature so the system knows what it is.

sections.title: Security and Interoperability
sections.content:
Mobile XMF content often has intellectual property rights. The RFC notes that copyright owners may apply security mechanisms externally to prevent unauthorized playback. Mobile XMF itself is not internally encrypted, and the format does not contain executable content. Mobile XMF players are designed to be robust against corrupted files, simply ignoring any unrecognized content.

The prl, minimum-pr, and total-pr parameters can serve a protective function by limiting resource consumption, preventing excessive memory usage during playback. Mobile XMF is based on the widely used MIDI specification and is designed for interoperability with a range of playback devices, from phones to handheld computers.
sections.plainLanguage: Music files might have copyrights, and some players could lock them with security. The format is safe because it doesn't run code, and players ignore parts they don't understand.

sections.title: Applications and Use
sections.content:
Mobile XMF is intended for music downloading, ringtones, and music messaging on portable devices. The compact size makes it practical for these uses. Applications include mobile phones, PDAs, and other handheld devices that need to play synthetic audio without the overhead of larger MIDI or audio file formats.

The intended usage is marked as COMMON, indicating that the format is suitable for widespread deployment. The MIDI Manufacturers Association maintains control and management of the namespace and the format specification through the change controller role specified in this RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: Mobile XMF is used for ringtones, downloaded music, and text message attachments on phones. It's much smaller than other music formats, so it fits on limited devices.
